name: Coffeehouse2Home Property Ledger
brief: Coffeehouse2Home is one software suite for a property-services company that does brokerage, house flipping, rentals, and field services, run by one shared Property Ledger: every property has a single record (ownership, address, status, full history) shared across all five domains. The real-estate CRM tracks contacts, buyer and seller leads, and a deal pipeline with stages; any listing, flip, or rental property can publish showing slots (private showings and open houses) that buyers book with email confirmation, reminders, calendar-sync stub, and a per-property showing history with buyer feedback. The flip manager tracks acquisitions, renovation budgets with line items, contractor bids, flip project phases, and job costing per property. The rental portfolio manages leases, tenants, rent roll with payment records, maintenance requests, vacancy tracking, and lease-renewal reminders. The field-ops suite turns work orders raised from any property (a flip task, a maintenance request, a buyer-requested repair) into crew task lists, rolls crew time sheets into weekly payroll with rates and overtime, and tracks material/supply lists with purchase records and reorder flags. Cross-domain data flows: work-order hours feed payroll and job cost, showings on flip or rental properties create CRM buyer leads, and every property's deals, flips, leases, and work orders accumulate on its shared ledger record.

## Mission
Coffeehouse2Home is one software suite for a property-services company that does brokerage, house flipping, rentals, and field services, run by one shared Property Ledger: every property has a single record (ownership, address, status, full history) shared across all five domains. The real-estate CRM tracks contacts, buyer and seller leads, and a deal pipeline with stages; any listing, flip, or rental property can publish showing slots (private showings and open houses) that buyers book with email confirmation, reminders, calendar-sync stub, and a per-property showing history with buyer feedback. The flip manager tracks acquisitions, renovation budgets with line items, contractor bids, flip project phases, and job costing per property. The rental portfolio manages leases, tenants, rent roll with payment records, maintenance requests, vacancy tracking, and lease-renewal reminders. The field-ops suite turns work orders raised from any property (a flip task, a maintenance request, a buyer-requested repair) into crew task lists, rolls crew time sheets into weekly payroll with rates and overtime, and tracks material/supply lists with purchase records and reorder flags. Cross-domain data flows: work-order hours feed payroll and job cost, showings on flip or rental properties create CRM buyer leads, and every property's deals, flips, leases, and work orders accumulate on its shared ledger record.

Provide a field-ops suite that turns work orders raised from any property (a flip task, a maintenance request, a buyer-requested repair) into crew task lists, rolls crew time sheets into weekly payroll with rates and overtime, and tracks material/supply lists with purchase records and reorder flags.

Feed cross-domain data: work-order hours must feed both payroll and job cost; showings on flip or rental properties must create CRM buyer leads; and every property's deals, flips, leases, and work orders must accumulate on its shared ledger record.
Annotate each showing history entry with buyer feedback only when feedback is supplied; otherwise the field is null, never inferred.
When a flip task, maintenance request, or buyer-requested repair is raised on a property, the corresponding work order must reference that originating record and that property's ledger record.
The shared Property Ledger history must be append-only: existing events are never mutated or deleted, only new events appended with timestamps.

Weekly payroll aggregation must compute regular hours and overtime hours separately using rates stored on the crew member or applicable record; missing rates cause the entry to be flagged, not silently defaulted.
edgeCases: A showing slot booked by two buyers at the same instant must result in exactly one confirmed booking and the other placed on a waitlist or returned as unavailable, never two confirmed bookings.
A property with zero showings, zero deals, zero flips, zero leases, and zero work orders must still return a valid ledger record with empty history arrays.
A buyer requesting a repair on a rental property must create both a CRM buyer lead and a field-ops work order tied to that property in one transaction.
A party (contact, tenant, contractor, crew member) may appear in multiple domains; the system must not deduplicate across domains unless the same ledger id is referenced.
A calendar-sync stub that is unreachable or returns no external id must not block the showing booking from being stored and confirmed; the sync attempt is recorded as attempted with a stub reference.
An email confirmation that fails to send must not roll back the stored showing; the failure is recorded on the showing record and surfaced for retry.
A work order with no associated hours cannot produce payroll or job-cost lines; it remains open until hours are recorded.
Overtime must be computed only above the applicable threshold; hours at or below threshold are regular, and the boundary value equals the threshold is regular.
A rent payment record for a tenant with no active lease must be rejected, not attached to the tenant without a lease.
A lease-renewal reminder must fire ahead of the lease end date; if the current time is already past the end date, the reminder is flagged as lapsed rather than suppressed silently.
A property cannot be listed for showing before its ledger status permits publication; statuses that disallow showings must reject the publish attempt with a stated reason.
Duplicate contact or lead creation with the same email or phone must be detected and returned as a duplicate reference rather than creating a second CRM record.
A purchase record for materials with quantity that pushes stock to or below the reorder threshold must set the reorder flag; quantity exactly at threshold sets the flag.
Combining work-order hours into payroll for a week with no timesheets must produce an empty payroll with explicit zero totals and no synthetic rows.
errorHandling: Invalid input (missing required property fields, unknown entity id, malformed dates) must be rejected with a validation error identifying the offending field, without partial writes.
Backend or datastore unavailable during a write must return a retryable failure and leave the shared ledger unchanged; no partial ledger event is appended.
Email confirmation failure must be recorded on the showing record with the failure reason and a retry marker; the showing remains confirmed.
Calendar-sync stub failure must be recorded as a sync attempt with the stub's error and must not abort the booking flow.

Partial write across domains (for example, showing stored but CRM buyer lead not created) must either be atomic or surfaced as a reconciliation entry on the ledger with the missing side marked pending.
Payroll run failure for a crew member due to missing rate must report that crew member and week as failed and exclude them from the payout total rather than assuming a default rate.
Timeout on any external step must be treated as a recorded attempt with a timeout marker and must not be retried indefinitely within the same request.
Attempting an operation on a property not present in the shared ledger must return not-found and must not implicitly create a property record.
Duplicate booking of an already-booked showing slot must return conflict, not a second confirmation.
Rejection of a contractor bid or a work-order cancellation must be an appended ledger event, never a deletion of the original record.
typeSignatures: recordShowingFeedback(bookingId: string, feedback: BuyerFeedback | null): Promise<ShowingBooking>
raiseWorkOrder(propertyId: string, source: WorkOrderSource, input: WorkOrderInput): Promise<WorkOrder>
dataFlow: Raw property input is validated for required ledger fields (ownership, address, status) and rejected on failure before persistence.
Valid property input creates a single PropertyLedgerRecord; all domain operations reference this propertyId.
CRM input creates contacts, buyer leads, seller leads, and deals; each is appended to the owning property's ledger history where a property is referenced.
A listing, flip, or rental property publishes showing slots onto its ledger record after a status check allows showings.
A buyer booking request targets a slot id, checks availability atomically, and on success creates a ShowingBooking tied to the property and buyer lead.
On successful booking, the system attempts email confirmation, schedules reminders, and calls the calendar-sync stub; each attempt outcome is recorded on the booking.
Buyer feedback, when supplied, is attached to the booking and appended to the property's showing history.
Flip tasks, maintenance requests, and buyer-requested repairs each raise a WorkOrder that references the originating record and the property ledger record.
WorkOrder hours from timesheets flow into both job cost for the property and weekly payroll aggregation.
Weekly payroll aggregates timesheets per crew member, splitting regular versus overtime against stored rates, and persists a PayrollRun.
Materials and supplies updates from purchases update stock and set reorder flags when quantity is at or below threshold.
Every cross-domain event (deals, flips, leases, work orders, purchases) is appended to the shared property ledger history in event order, never mutated in place.
Failure path: any step that fails to persist or times out records a ledger event describing the attempted action and failure, so the shared ledger remains the single source of truth.
negativeConstraints: DO NOT create a second property record for the same property; all domains must share one PropertyLedgerRecord.
DO NOT mutate or delete existing ledger events; only append new events.
DO NOT invent external platforms, dependencies, error codes, or users beyond the brief and the calendar-sync stub.
DO NOT allow two confirmed bookings for the same showing slot.
DO NOT send a buyer lead, work order, payroll line, or job-cost line without linking it to the originating property ledger record where the brief states a property source.
DO NOT default missing payroll rates; flag and exclude instead.
DO NOT block a showing confirmation on email or calendar-sync stub success.
DO NOT roll back a stored showing on email confirmation failure; record the failure and keep the booking.
DO NOT attach a rent payment to a tenant without an active lease.
DO NOT publish showing slots for a property whose status disallows showings.
DO NOT fabricate buyer feedback; leave null when not supplied.
DO NOT deduplicate contacts or leads across domains unless the same ledger id is referenced.
